MAGTUTULOY-TULOY PA ANG ULAN? ☔️

PAGASA issued a thunderstorm advisory late Tuesday night, July 8, following heavy rains that caused flooding in several parts of Metro Manila and nearby provinces.

In its 11:28 p.m. bulletin, the weather bureau said moderate to heavy rainshowers with lightning and strong winds are expected within the next two hours over Metro Manila, Pampanga, Bulacan, Tarlac, Quezon, Laguna, Rizal, and Nueva Ecija.

Meanwhile, heavy to intense rainfall is currently being experienced in parts of Zambales, Batangas, Cavite, and Bataan, which may persist and affect nearby areas.

📸 PAGASA

Just my curiosity. 

Malaysia’s Risky Balancing Act: Neutral Without Power in a World on Fire.

Look around. The world’s changing and not in a slow, peaceful kind of way. It’s cracking. Splitting. Shifting.
On one side, you’ve got the U.S. and its crew tightening their grip on tech, trade, and military alliances. On the other, China, Russia, BRICS redrawing the rulebook, flipping the old world order on its head.
And smack in the middle?
Malaysia.
Still trying to play nice. Still pretending neutrality is a real strategy in 2025.
Still believing we can trade with China by day, talk democracy with the West at night, shout about Gaza at global forums, flirt with BRICS over lunch and somehow not get burned.
Is that really how the world works now?
Because if you peek back at history, real history, not the sanitized version, it tells a different story.
Neutrality?
Ask Belgium how that went in World War II.
Ask the Netherlands. Ask Malaya.
They tried to sit out the chaos. Play it cool.
Result? Invaded. Exploited. Flattened.
Morals didn’t stop bombs. Speeches didn’t block tanks. And back then, we were a British colony didn’t save us either. The Japanese walked right through the front door. We were unready, unarmed, unprotected.
Fast forward. Different era, same false comfort.
Anwar Ibrahim wants to play diplomat. Bridge-builder. Non-aligned peace talker.
Respectfully, that’s cute. But here’s the uncomfortable truth:
We have no real military deterrence.
Our economy? Dangling between China’s markets and the West’s tech.
Our neighbors? They’ve quietly picked sides.
Philippines = U.S.
Singapore = West-leaning.
Cambodia, Laos = Beijing’s pocket.
And us?
Still holding up the non-alignment banner… with no backup plan.
No food security.
No tech independence.
No real supply chain control.
If global systems break, who helps us?
If the world fractures for real, who do we run to?
What fortress do we hide in when all we’ve built is a stage?
Sure, we speak loud on Palestine.
Sure, we join BRICS Zoom calls.
But loud speeches don’t stop hunger.
Or cyberattacks.
Or drone strikes.
Or Trade War. 
So here's the question nobody wants to ask:
Are we actually ready for anything?
Or are we just hoping the fire won’t reach us?
Maybe Anwar thinks diplomacy will save us.
But what if diplomacy fails?
What if everyone stops playing nice?
Because when the world burns and it just might bridges don’t survive. Fortresses do.
So what are we building, Malaysia?
A moral voice with no shield?
A paper tiger with great quotes?
Or a nation ready to take a hit and stay standing?
History won’t remember what we said.
It’ll remember whether we were ready.
And whether we Survived… or froze.
"Anything is possible.
I’m not asking you to pick a side, but think about it — when you play too much, you end up burned out.
Salam 25%🫣
#3rdforce #HIRUK

data.raw_text:
Kumusta ang panahon sa inyong lugar?

Sa inilabas na thunderstorm advisory ng PAGASA kaninang 11:28 P.M., makararanas ng moderate to heavy rainshowers na may kasamang kidlat at malakas na hangin ang Metro Manila, Pampanga, Bulacan, Tarlac, Quezon, Laguna, Rizal at Nueva Ecija sa susunod na dalawang oras.

Heavy to intense rainshowers na may kasamang kidlat at malakas na hangin ang kasalukuyang nararanasan sa Zambales (Iba, Palauig, Masinloc, San Antonio, Subic, Olongapo), Batangas (Nasugbu), Cavite (Maragondon, Ternate) at Bataan (Morong) na maaaring magpatuloy sa loob ng dalawang oras at makakaapekto rin sa katabing mga lugar.

Ang ilang parte ng Metro Manila, binaha dahil sa malakas na pag-ulan kanina.

Lahat ay pinagiingat sa mga panganib na maaaring idulot ng pag-ulan, kabilang na ang mga baha at mga landslide.

Panoorin ang ulat: https://t.co/NV5A7lGQmk

Courtesy: PAGASA’s PANaHON Interactive Weather Map
